Neither proof imports the source explicit W_gamma machinery.

contents.name: Proposition 1.1: the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis indexed by paths, and products of successive central idempotents along a path as rank-one projections
Proposition 1.4: the spectrum of a restriction is simple if and only if the centralizer of the subgroup algebra is commutative
contents.reason: The page already has the multiplicity-free restriction rule as a published supplier, so this general simplicity criterion is used neither as a statement nor as a proof step here.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1: the centralizer Z(C[S_n], C[S_{n-1}]) is commutative
Lemma 2.2: every element of S_n is conjugate to its inverse by an element of S_{n-1}
Lemma 2.3: an algebra over C with involution is commutative if all real elements are self-conjugate
Theorem 2.4: the general commutative-centralizer criterion for a star-algebra with an invariant basis
contents.reason: The S_n-specific coefficient-comparison proof of Theorem 2.1 is used directly, so the general criterion for star-algebras with an orthonormal-type basis is never invoked on this page.

contents.name: Theorem 2.5: Z(n) is contained in the algebra generated by Z(n-1) and X_n
Corollary 2.6: GZ(n) is generated by the Young-Jucys-Murphy elements X_1,...,X_n
Remark 2.7: the YJM elements do not lie in the corresponding centres, so the natural basis is non-central
contents.reason: The observation is ancillary to SYMR-5 and no proof needs noncentrality. The source wording has small-rank exceptions: X1=0 and X2 are central. For k=3, conjugating X3=(13)+(23) by (13) gives (13)+(12), so X3 is noncentral. The local spectral route instead uses central transposition sums and their successive differences.

contents.name: Theorem 2.8: the centralizer Z(C[S_n], C[S_{n-1}]) is generated by Z(C[S_{n-1}]) and X_n
Theorem 2.9: the branching C[S_1] subset ... subset C[S_n] is simple (multiplicity-free restriction)
Corollary 2.10: GZ(n) is a maximal commutative subalgebra and the Young basis is determined up to scalars
Relations (3.2)-(3.3): s_i X_j = X_j s_i for j not in {i,i+1} and s_i X_i + 1 = X_{i+1} s_i
Section 3: the local algebra H(2) generated by Y_1 = X_{n-1}, Y_2 = X_n, s = s_n, and the locality of the generator action
Propositions 3.1-3.2: the action of s_k affects only the k-th level of the branching graph and C[S_n] is generated by C[S_{n-1}] with H(2)
Remark 3.3 and the degenerate affine Hecke algebra H(n)
contents.reason: The abstract degenerate affine Hecke algebra is neither needed for the ordinary complex statements proved here nor minted as a separate algebraic object on this page.

contents.name: Definition of the set Cont(n) of content vectors by the predecessor and collision conditions
Proposition 4.1(1)-(3): weights of the Young basis, distinctness of adjacent weights, admissible transpositions and the sign cases
Formula (4.2): the explicit two-dimensional matrices of s_i, X_i, X_{i+1} in the eigenbasis of the local algebra
Theorem 5.1: every element of the spectrum Spec(n) is a content vector
Lemma 5.2: a fragment (a, a+1, a) cannot occur in the spectrum, by the Coxeter relation s_i s_{i+1} s_i = s_{i+1} s_i s_{i+1}
Proposition 5.3: the content vector map is a bijection from standard tableaux onto Cont(n)
Lemma 5.4 and Corollary 5.5: admissible transpositions connect tableaux with the same diagram and preserve the spectrum
Remarks 5.6-5.7: geodesic chains of admissible transpositions and adic transformations
contents.reason: These remarks concern the metric geometry of the Young graph and infinite tableaux; no statement on this page uses the geodesic or adic properties.

contents.name: Theorem 5.8: the Young graph is the branching graph and Spec(n) = Cont(n) with matching equivalence relations
Proposition 6.1: existence of a basis with the seminormal formulas s_i v_T = v_T' + r^{-1} v_T and s_i v_T' = (1 - r^{-2}) v_T - r^{-1} v_T'
Proposition 6.2 with formula (6.5): the orthonormal Young basis and the orthogonal two-by-two block
Remark 6.3: highest-weight terminology for the row-major tableau
contents.reason: The highest-weight terminology is not used by any statement on the page; the row-major tableau appears only as the phasing anchor for the seminormal formulas.

contents.name: Corollary 7.1: the multiplicity of an irreducible in a restriction, deduced from the branching theorem
Proposition 7.2: the inverse image of the scalars under the deletion projection meets the centralizer in the span of 1 and X_n
contents.reason: The deletion projection and the inverse spectrum of virtual permutations are not part of this page, whose centralizer statements are proved by the edge-separation argument.

contents.name: Theorem 7.3: the generalized centralizer Z(l,k) is generated by centres, the permuted group and the YJM elements
contents.reason: The two-sided generalization for k > 1 is a later structural topic; only the k = 1 case is needed and proved here, and no commissioned claim depends on the general form.

contents.name: Section 8: the Murnaghan-Nakayama rule from the inductive construction
contents.reason: The character recursion is the subject of the separate rim-hooks and Murnaghan-Nakayama page of the symmetric-group plan, which owns its proof and examples.
